design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 of patient_balance_and_coverage_resolution (billing). Frozen 2026-09-23 14:15 EDT.

[Step 0 — pre-check, draw, claim]
draw_counts.py --task 0 printed: prerequisite_problems=2, problems=3, factor_counts=[4, 6, 5]. Assignment: pre-placement statement 4, final-notice paydown 6 (root), card-on-file charge 5.
Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0). Claimed here: billing_ext_card_on_file_charge (target charge_card_on_file_381e2993, agent), billing_ext_pre_placement_statement (target issue_account_statement_de3ca581, agent), billing_ext_final_notice_paydown (target pay_final_notice_balance_8381dcc2, owner=user). Left for task 1 (draw: 1 prerequisite problem, factor counts [4, 6]): the credit-refund write (billing_refund_issued) and the replacement of returned check/ACH payments (a second, distinct customer payment), i.e. an independent refund tree on a different account situation (active insured account with a credit), so task 1 has its own root, its own customer write and its own load-bearing value_input edge.
Gate-driven scope decision (recorded at Step 0): every base eligibility gate whose applies_to hits a write's subject must be evidenced. billing_adjustment_posted carries 9 gates across 4 base policies, one of them (billing_retro_coverage_rebill.coverage_in_force_on_dos) mixed-authority on a one-field correlation key and therefore unsatisfiable; billing_charge_posted carries the late-fee time gate and waiver_on_file at once. So no problem of this difficulty writes an adjustment or a charge; problems are carried by billing_payment_posted, billing_statement_issued and billing_refund_issued.
Design thesis: surface goal "what do I pay today so the account does not go to collections, and I pay it now" -> policy prerequisite chain (the paydown figure waits on a statement dated no earlier than the last charge posting; that statement's balance waits on the most recent encounter carrying its card-on-file payment) -> core computation (good-faith share of the statement balance less the reinstatable part of a defaulted plan's release) -> observable terminal state (card-on-file payment entry, statement entry, card payment entry, account back to active with final_notice_date cleared). Depth: 2 hops of prerequisite. Breadth: 15 factors reading the ledger, the account's coverage/verification fields, the appointment product (visit types, documentation window), the payplan product (default, release, reinstatement window) and the membership product (tier discount, activation date).

[Problem-tree card]
Root: billing_ext_final_notice_paydown (the customer's ask). Edges:
(1) paydown -> pre-placement statement: kind value_input, gate statement_balance, form state. Prerequisite sentence (paydown's own rule, negated direction, as a collections desk states a release it withholds): "The final-notice paydown is not fixed until the account's most recent statement is dated no earlier than its most recent charge posting." Four-point test: ordering connective "not ... until"; record-visible state (statement date vs charge posting date on the ledger); no tool/id/code token; hard requirement at the exact scope of the condition (the most recent statement vs the most recent charge). Exactly one write of this difficulty creates a statement entry (the pre-placement statement), so the reader can resolve the hop: sentence + ledger (last statement 2026-09-03, last charge 2026-09-19) + the statement policy's own rule ("An account in precollection whose most recent charge was posted after its most recent statement is issued a pre-placement statement on the handling date ...") -> issue the pre-placement statement. Unresolved at opening: st3.txn_date = 2026-09-03 < late2/e5_coi/e5_nc txn_date = 2026-09-19. Load-bearing: skipping the statement gives paydown 327.58 instead of 521.09.
(2) pre-placement statement -> card-on-file charge: kind value_input, gate owed, form state. Prerequisite sentence (statement rule, affirmative direction, as a billing office states a figure that rests on prior postings): "On an account whose tier requires a card on file, the pre-placement statement balance is fixed only after the most recent encounter carries a card-on-file payment." Four-point test: "only after"; record-visible state (a card_on_file payment entry on the encounter); no tool/id/code token; scope limited to card-on-file tiers. Exactly one write of this difficulty posts a card_on_file payment (the card-on-file charge). Unresolved at opening: no billing_payment_posted row with payment_method card_on_file carries ENC-21866604 (the only card_on_file rows carry ENC-21302276 and ENC-21574418). Load-bearing: skipping the charge gives statement 1250.25 instead of 1617.73 and paydown 586.23.
Topological order (unique, chain): card-on-file charge -> statement -> paydown. Charter direction mix: one affirmative ("only after"), one negated ("not ... until") prerequisite sentence. Customer write: the paydown (owner=user); the in-person semantics are real (she pays with her own card on the secure line; the agent never takes card numbers). The persona never names a prerequisite; the tools validate none.

[Base-invariant card]
card-on-file charge and paydown write billing_payment_posted, governed only by billing_payment_application; its single gate designated_encounter ("A payment is applied to a specific encounter only when the patient names that encounter's encounter number.") is retired by an explicit overwrite in both extended policies (their rules fix the charge the entry is posted against), so base_preconditions carry billing_payment_application as policy_scope. The allocation-order clause and the HDHP card-on-file clause of the same base policy are also declared superseded (card-on-file charge) and the "paying it below collections_min_balance_usd ... returns the account to active" clauses of billing_statement_escalation and billing_collections_recall are declared superseded by the paydown method sentence. The statement writes billing_statement_issued, governed by billing_statement_escalation (gate statement_only_when_billable: status active or precollection; evidence billing_accounts.status = precollection, correlated by billing_account_id) and billing_itemized_statement (no gate; policy_scope). No time gate applies to these subjects, so temporal_feasibility is empty; the escalation clock is consistent: final notice 2026-09-03, placement allowed from 2026-10-03, so the account is not placeable at frozen time.

[Business-object card]
Account 4952bfb5-5537-4dcc-a702-6ba4721e1291 (one non-closed account). Card-on-file object: encounter ENC-21866604 (Advanced Imaging Appointment 2026-08-27): deductible 412.75 (2026-09-10), coinsurance 690.00 (2026-09-19), non-covered 96.40 (2026-09-19); the charge posts against the coinsurance line (largest deductible/coinsurance line). Statement object: the whole account balance owed 2418.10 at opening (charges 4997.10 - payments 2579.00), rows included: every charge/payment; plan balance excluded only for active/delinquent plans (the plan is defaulted, so 0.00). Paydown object: the statement's balance less the reinstatable part of the plan release (420.00 released 2026-08-26 on ENC-21302276's enrolled charge, less one reinstatement installment 105.00). The paydown posts against the open charge with the earliest date of service (2026-03-24, 1380.00 deductible, open 420.00). Settled rows: membership dues 869.00 paid 2026-02-01; plan installments 1-2 applied to the enrolled charge; card-on-file charges 750.00 x 2 on the two older encounters.

[Factor card — card-on-file charge (5 factors; result 322.52)]
notice_anchor (method, the anchor the notice clock starts from): tier = precollection -> notice counted from the date of service 2026-08-27, both lines covered (1102.75); baseline (notice counted from each line's own posting date) -> 46.52. Near-miss: the coinsurance line posted 2026-09-19 is 4 days old by its posting date and would be excluded under the standard anchor.
deductible_ceiling (parameter; its two conditions are both fields of the account row, so it is not counted as multi-source): 116.30 remaining, verified 34 days ago -> deductible counts 116.30; baseline full deductible -> 400.0.
visit_type_cap (parameter, cross-difficulty appointment): Advanced Imaging -> 1000.00; baseline tier cap 750.00 -> 300.0.
plan_history_share (parameter, cross-difficulty payplan, multi-source): defaulted 2026-08-26 and 420.00 released inside six months -> 50 percent; baseline 100 -> 645.04. Near-miss: the plan also has two missed installments (tier b), but the default tier is stated as disjoint by its own condition and takes precedence only because the plan is no longer active or delinquent.
membership_hold (parameter, cross-difficulty membership): active Essential membership, imaging visit -> imaging_discount_pct 20 held back; baseline 0 -> 403.15.
Whole baseline (computation document only): 412.75.

[Factor card — pre-placement statement (4 factors; result 1617.73)]
statement_lead_time (method): HDHP with card on file -> lines of ENC-21866604 posted fewer than 5 days ago without a card-on-file payment are left off: the non-covered 96.40 is left off, the coinsurance line (charged at step 11) is shown; baseline shows every line -> 1714.13.
deductible_above_remaining (parameter): 412.75 open vs 116.30 remaining (verified 34 days ago) -> 296.45 left off; baseline -> 1914.18.
no_show_documentation_window (parameter, cross-difficulty appointment): no-show 2026-09-17, Specialist Consultation window 7 days, first no-show waived by that visit type -> 75.00 left off; baseline -> 1692.73. Near-miss: the February no-show was waived as a first offense and carries no billing charge, so it is not the fee concerned.
post_notice_late_fee (parameter): two late fees in 12 months, the latest (2026-09-19) after the final notice, account 91 months old -> 10.00 left off; baseline -> 1627.73. Near-miss: the 2026-08-20 late fee predates the notice and stays on.
Whole baseline: 2095.58.

[Factor card — final-notice paydown (6 factors; result 521.09)]
paydown_method (method): no returned payment, tenure 91 months >= 36 -> good-faith share; baseline (base - 50.00 + 0.01) -> 1252.74.
tenure_percentage (parameter): 60 <= 91 < 120 months -> 50; baseline 60 -> 651.37.
card_on_file_reduction (parameter): card-on-file payment this month (step 11) -> -10; baseline 0 -> 651.37.
membership_reduction (parameter, cross-difficulty membership): active since 2026-02-01 (7 months) -> -10; baseline 0 -> 651.37.
late_fee_addition (parameter): two late fees in 12 months -> +10; baseline 0 -> 390.82.
reinstatable_plan_release (method, cross-difficulty payplan, multi-source): defaulted 28 days ago (window 30), 6-Month tier -> 420.00 - 105.00 = 315.00 left out; baseline -> 647.09.
Whole baseline: 1567.74.
Every declared factor sits off its fall-through tier on this world and moves its result (check_compute factor sensitivity); no factor reads a stamp that names its own outcome.

[Why initial_state rows exist]
Ledger rows: the three statements and the post-notice charges establish the escalation state and the statement prerequisite; the ENC-21866604 lines are the card-on-file object; the older card-on-file charges and plan installments make the history real and are the near-misses of the card-on-file state (card_on_file rows on other encounters); membership dues rows reconcile the membership product; late fees drive two factors. Appointments carry the visit types (cap tier, hold tier, documentation window). Appointment events record the assessed no-show fee and the earlier waived first offense. Payment plan and its ledger carry default date, release amount and installment amount. Automatic clauses checked: no late fee is due beyond the two posted (the 2026-09-03 statement's late-fee day is 2026-10-18); no placement is due before 2026-10-03; the plan is defaulted, so no installment falls due; the membership is annual and paid; no refund obligation (no credit).

[Persona design]
Nora Gallagher, practical and rattled, lunch-break caller. Volunteers only the surface goal (pay now what keeps it from collections, by her own debit card). Gives name and phone to locate, DOB and MRN to verify, only when asked. Passive facts only on request: summer/August imaging, missed 2026-09-17 visit (son sick, nothing sent), old plan stopped when her card expired end of June, Essential membership since February. Passive reactions: consents when told a card-on-file charge or an updated statement must go out; declines any plan offer; runs the handed-over payment with the agent's figures; ends when told the payment went through and the account is active; asks for one re-check if a figure surprises her but never supplies math. No template labels; no prerequisite named.

[Standard solution and recomputation]
Reads: customer, identity, account, ledger, appointments, appointment events, plan, plan ledger, membership, membership ledger. Writes in topological order: step 11 charge_card_on_file_381e2993(account, coinsurance line of ENC-21866604, 322.52); step 13 issue_account_statement_de3ca581(account, 1617.73, 1); step 15 (handed over) pay_final_notice_balance_8381dcc2(account, 2026-03-24 charge, 521.09).
Verification code: the authoring harness replays the gold writes with the real tools on initial_state and evaluates each policy compute on the handling-time world with check_compute's own build_env/eval_compute (the same entry point the COMPUTE gate uses): card-on-file charge 322.52 (baseline 412.75); statement 1617.73 (baseline 2095.58; without step 11: 1250.25); paydown 521.09 (baseline 1567.74; without step 13: 327.58; without step 11: 586.23).

[Draft recomputation from the visible context]
Using only the rules, the tool schemas, the finder returns and the persona: the paydown rule says the figure waits on a statement dated no earlier than the last charge (ledger: 2026-09-03 vs 2026-09-19) -> the statement rule (precollection account, charge after last statement -> issue the pre-placement statement) -> which on a card-on-file tier waits on the most recent encounter's card-on-file payment (none on ENC-21866604) -> the card-on-file rule. Computing each at its handling time reproduces 322.52, 1617.73 and 521.09; the posting sentences fix the lines charged and paid against; statement_sequence 1 follows from the series-restart sentence. No second reading was found.

[Closure]
policy -> tool -> computation -> GT call -> terminal state: card-on-file charge -> charge_card_on_file_381e2993 -> computations[0] step 11 -> new card_on_file payment entry, balance owed down; pre-placement statement -> issue_account_statement_de3ca581 -> computations[1] step 13 -> new statement entry, last_statement_date 2026-09-23; final-notice paydown -> pay_final_notice_balance_8381dcc2 -> computations[2] step 15 -> card payment entry, status active, final_notice_date cleared. charter_scope, required_documents and computations all list the same three policies in that order. The whole tree resolves under one frozen_time with synchronous writes; nothing waits on a real-world event.


[Revision r2 — policy-task audit r1 closed item by item]
F-2 (card-on-file method factor was a threshold substitution): symptom covered_lines selected lines by 0 / notice / 2 x notice days; root cause a single selector with different thresholds labelled method; change: the factor is now notice_anchor, whose tiers choose the date the notice clock starts from (date of service for precollection accounts, the encounter's first posting for paperless accounts, each line's own posting date otherwise), the anchor family of method factors; the mail tier (O-6) is gone. Re-run: 322.52 unchanged, notice_anchor baseline 46.52, whole baseline 412.75, COMPUTE OK.
F-1 (returned payments counted without the check/ACH qualifier): the paydown's returned_12m now counts only reversals with payment_method check or ach (no reversal row on this world, so 521.09 is unchanged).
T0-O2: edge_load_bearing[1] now states the replay protocol (statement replayed at its gold argument -> 586.23; recomputed -> 420.86).
T0-O3: deductible_ceiling is no longer described as multi-source; the task's multi-source factors are plan_history_share, membership_hold, no_show_documentation_window, post_notice_late_fee and reinstatable_plan_release.
O-9: the statement rule now defines the no-show fee's open part as its amount less payments and adjustments, matching fee_open.
user_scenario:
You are Nora Gallagher, 43, a dental hygienist in Dublin, Ohio, calling Linden Ridge Medical Group's Patient Services line on your lunch break. You sound a little rattled but polite and practical. A letter came saying your account is in its final notice and could be sent to an outside collection agency, and you want to deal with it today. In your own words: you want to know how much you have to pay right now to keep it from going to collections, and you want to pay that amount today with your own debit card. You are not asking for anything else, and you do not know how the office works out its numbers.
When the agent asks who you are, you give your full name, Nora Gallagher, and your cell number, 6145552586. If they need to confirm your identity you give your date of birth, 1983-07-19, and the medical record number printed on your statements, LR2471936; you only give these when asked, one or two at a time, never all at once. You do not remember any account numbers or amounts beyond the fact that the letter looked like 'over a thousand dollars'; if the agent asks you to confirm a figure you say you do not have the letter in front of you and trust what they see on the account.
Only if the agent asks about your visits: you had imaging done over the summer and at the end of August, and you missed an orthopedic appointment on September 17 because your son was home sick; you have not sent anything to the office about that missed visit. Only if asked about the old payment plan: you know it stopped going through after your old debit card expired at the end of June and you have not dealt with it since. Only if asked about the Linden membership: yes, you still have the Essential membership you joined in February.
If the agent tells you something has to be charged to the card you keep on file, or that an updated statement has to go out, before they can give you the figure, you say that is fine and let them go ahead. If the agent offers to set up, restart or reinstate a payment plan, you decline politely; you would rather pay today. When the agent tells you the amount and hands you the secure payment step, you complete it yourself with the account and the charge reference the agent gives you and exactly the amount the agent quoted, and you read back the confirmation you get. Once the agent tells you the payment went through and the account is back to active, you thank them and end the call. If the agent says you owe a different amount than you expected, you do not argue about the math; you only ask them to double-check it against the account once.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (paydown <- statement <- card-on-file charge): each problem has exactly one prerequisite, so the only topological order is card-on-file charge, statement, paydown. No two writes are parallel, so no alternative order needs to be proved equal.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the statement write (step 13) leaves the 2026-09-03 final-notice statement (1133.95) as the most recent statement: payment_amount_usd becomes 327.58 instead of 521.09, and the terminal DB lacks the statement entry.

Skipping the card-on-file charge (step 11) and replaying every other gold call with its gold arguments: statement_amount_usd recomputes to 1250.25 instead of 1617.73 (the uncharged coinsurance line stays inside the lead time and is left off, and the balance owed is 322.52 higher); with the statement call replayed at its gold argument 1617.73 the paydown recomputes to 586.23 instead of 521.09 (only its card-on-file reduction tier changes, from 10 to 5 points); if the statement were first recomputed to 1250.25 the paydown would be 420.86. The terminal DB also lacks the card-on-file payment.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the final-notice paydown ('how much you have to pay right now to keep it from going to collections'). It never mentions the card on file, a statement, the encounter lines or the plan release as something to do; the only lines about a card-on-file charge or an updated statement are passive consent reactions that fire after the agent says so ('If the agent tells you something has to be charged to the card you keep on file, or that an updated statement has to go out ... you say that is fine').
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py: pay_final_notice_balance_8381dcc2 creates the payment entry and updates the account with whatever arguments it gets; it never reads statements or card-on-file payments and never returns an error. issue_account_statement_de3ca581 creates the statement entry without looking at card-on-file payments. charge_card_on_file_381e2993 checks neither status nor notice. Skipping a prerequisite therefore only shows up as a different terminal hash.
